data.rationale: Use FastAPI with the standard-library sqlite3 driver. Only repository.py and db.py know SQL. Consequences: Zero-setup local runs and tests; moving to a client/server database replaces two modules. Write throughput is limited to one writer.
data.title: ADR-1: FastAPI on SQLite behind a repository seam

data.rationale: Generate 7 random base62 characters from the OS CSPRNG; rely on the primary key for uniqueness and retry a collision up to 5 times. Consequences: No coordination between instances is needed. Collision probability stays negligible until billions of links; exhaustion surfaces as a retryable 503.
data.title: ADR-2: Random base62 codes with database-enforced uniqueness

data.rationale: Answer GET /{code} with 307 and Cache-Control: no-store. Consequences: Accurate counts and immediate effect of deletion, at the cost of one extra round trip per visit.
data.title: ADR-3: 307 redirects that are never cached

data.rationale: DELETE marks the link inactive; redirects then answer 410 Gone. Consequences: Codes are never reused, which prevents old links from silently pointing somewhere new.
data.title: ADR-4: Soft delete

data.rationale: Keep an ordered list of migrations; apply the pending ones transactionally on start and record them in schema_migrations. Consequences: A new instance and an upgraded instance converge on the same schema. Rolling back a release requires migrations to be backward compatible.
data.title: ADR-5: Forward-only migrations applied at start-up
